shortDescription: Repair the Waystones Warp Stone with amethyst in an anvil (free while the Free Anvil Repair module is enabled)
oneLiner: Amethyst shards repair the Waystones Warp Stone in an anvil - 25% of its maximum durability per shard, costing one XP level per shard, or nothing at all while the Free Anvil Repair module is enabled.

optionalMods.whatItAdds: Supplies the default target item `waystones:warp_stone`, the damageable teleport item the module makes repairable. There is no compile dependency, no ModList.isLoaded check, no shouldInitialize gate and no waystones entry in the bundle's neoforge.mods.toml (grep -i waystone -> no hit): with the module enabled the AnvilUpdateEvent handler is registered either way, it just never matches because the configured id fails BuiltInRegistries.ITEM.containsKey, so the module is silently inert. Nothing breaks without Waystones, and target_item can point at any other installed damageable item instead.
optionalMods.evidence: src/main/java/net/geraldhofbauer/vanillaplusadditions/modules/waystone_amethyst_repair/config/WaystoneAmethystRepairConfig.java:19 (DEFAULT_TARGET_ITEM) + .../WaystoneAmethystRepairModule.java:133-145 (resolveTargetItem; containsKey check at :137, "module inert" debug log at :140-142); handler registration unconditional at WaystoneAmethystRepairModule.java:61; no waystones dependency in src/main/resources/META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml

events: net.neoforged.neoforge.event.AnvilUpdateEvent (WaystoneAmethystRepairModule.onAnvilUpdate, @SubscribeEvent at default priority; the module instance is registered on NeoForge.EVENT_BUS in onInitialize, WaystoneAmethystRepairModule.java:59-63). It is the module's only event subscription.

configKeys.range: no spec range; validator requires a String that ResourceLocation.tryParse accepts (WaystoneAmethystRepairConfig.java:44-45)
configKeys.effect: The damageable item made repairable by this module (Waystones Warp Stone by default). Resolved lazily by registry id and re-resolved whenever the string changes, so it takes effect without a restart; if the id is not installed (or unparsable) the module stays inert instead of erroring.

configKeys.range: no spec range; per-entry validator requires a String that ResourceLocation.tryParse accepts (WaystoneAmethystRepairConfig.java:50-52)
configKeys.effect: Item ids accepted as repair material in the anvil (amethyst shards by default). Entries are trimmed and resolved into a Set<Item>; entries whose item is not installed are skipped with a debug-only log line. Any listed material repairs at the same rate - there is no per-material weighting.

How much of the item's maximum durability a single material unit restores, in percent (vanilla material repairs use 25). Applied as perUnit = max(1, maxDamage * percent / 100) with integer division, and units are consumed one at a time until the item is undamaged or the material stack runs out; the number of consumed units is both the material cost and (unless free_anvil_repair is enabled) the XP level cost.

notes:
SOURCE FOOTPRINT (verified by find + grep): the whole module is TWO files - modules/waystone_amethyst_repair/WaystoneAmethystRepairModule.java (173 lines) and modules/waystone_amethyst_repair/config/WaystoneAmethystRepairConfig.java (86 lines). A grep for DeferredRegister / KeyMapping / Dist. / Minecraft.getInstance / registerCommand / ModList / shouldInitialize / isEnabledByDefault / @EventBusSubscriber / LootTableLoadEvent / AddReloadListener / Packet / Payload over both files returns ZERO hits: no registries, no items, no blocks, no entities, no commands, no keybinds, no packets, no mod gate, no enabled-by-default override (Module.java:73 default true applies), no shouldInitialize override (AbstractModule.java:112 default true applies). No mixin (grep "waystone" in vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json -> nothing), no standalone class (src/main/java/.../standalone/ has no waystone_amethyst_repair package) and no entry in build.gradle's standaloneModules (grep "waystone" build.gradle -> 0 hits), so this module ships ONLY inside the bundle jar. No lang keys (grep -i waystone in assets/vanillaplusadditions/lang/en_us.json -> nothing), no TODO/FIXME, and the only reference outside its own package is the import + registerModule call in VanillaPlusAdditions.java:19 and :175.

DOC STATE: there is no docs/modules/waystone_amethyst_repair.md yet - a doc writer starts from scratch. The existing prose is README.md:134-135 (heading + one paragraph) and the optional-mods table row README.md:232. CHANGELOG.md:940 documents the module under the header [1.0.0-beta.33] (CHANGELOG.md:938), which matches the tag.

HOW IT WORKS (everything lives in WaystoneAmethystRepairModule): onInitialize (lines 59-63) does nothing but NeoForge.EVENT_BUS.register(this) plus an info log. onAnvilUpdate (lines 69-91) bails unless (a) the module is enabled, (b) left and right are both non-empty, (c) left.isDamageableItem() and left.getDamageValue() > 0, (d) left matches the resolved target_item, (e) right's item is in the resolved repair_materials set, (f) the event carries no rename. applyRepair (lines 98-122): perUnit = Math.max(1, left.getMaxDamage() * repair_percent_per_unit / 100) - INTEGER division, so e.g. a 64-durability item at 25% gets 16/unit, and any item whose maxDamage*percent/100 rounds to 0 still repairs 1 point per unit. It then copies left and consumes units one at a time, each restoring min(remaining damage, perUnit), until the copy is undamaged or the right stack runs out, and finishes with setOutput(result), setMaterialCost(unitsUsed) and setCost(free ? 0 : unitsUsed) - i.e. 1 XP level per consumed shard unless free_anvil_repair is enabled.

DEAD BRANCH: the `if (unitsUsed == 0) return;` guard at lines 108-110 can never fire. onAnvilUpdate already guarantees left.getDamageValue() > 0 and right non-empty (count >= 1), and perUnit >= 1, so the while loop always runs at least once. (Same shape as free_anvil_repair's unreachable damagePerUnit <= 0 guard.)

RESULT IS A PLAIN COPY: result = left.copy() with only the damage value lowered - no component is added, removed or recomputed. Enchantments, custom name and the existing REPAIR_COST (prior-work) value survive untouched, and REPAIR_COST is never incremented, so repeated repairs never get more expensive and gear that already shows "Too Expensive!" stays repairable. VERIFIED OUTSIDE THE REPO (the repo checks in no Minecraft/NeoForge sources): in the NeoForge version this build uses (gradle.properties:21 neo_version=21.0.167) CommonHooks.onAnvilChange (neoforge-21.0.167-sources.jar, CommonHooks.java:683-694) writes the event's output into the result slot, calls container.setMaximumCost(e.getCost()), sets repairItemCountCost = e.getMaterialCost() and returns false; the patched AnvilMenu.createResult (decompiled 1.21.1 sources in ~/.gradle/caches/ng_execute/.../net/minecraft/world/inventory/AnvilMenu.java:130) does `if (!CommonHooks.onAnvilChange(...)) return;`, so vanilla's entire cost/penalty computation is skipped for this combination.

PRECONDITION NOBODY CONTROLS: AnvilUpdateEvent is only fired INSIDE vanilla's `if (!itemstack.isEmpty() && EnchantmentHelper.canStoreEnchantments(itemstack))` branch (AnvilMenu.java:122 + :130). canStoreEnchantments == stack.has(ENCHANTMENTS) (EnchantmentHelper.java:83-85), and DataComponents.COMMON_ITEM_COMPONENTS (DataComponents.java:233-240) puts ENCHANTMENTS on EVERY item by default, so in practice this is always true - but an item whose ENCHANTMENTS component a mod removed would never reach this module at all.

MATERIAL CONSUMPTION: setMaterialCost(unitsUsed) becomes AnvilMenu.repairItemCountCost; on take, vanilla shrinks the right stack by that amount only when count > cost, otherwise it clears the whole right slot (AnvilMenu.onTake:84-95). Since unitsUsed <= right.getCount(), the two branches produce the same outcome here. onTake also charges giveExperienceLevels(-cost) for non-creative players.

RENAMING FALLS BACK TO VANILLA: isRenaming (lines 164-172) returns true when a non-blank name differs from left.getHoverName().getString(), or when a blank name is sent for an item that HAS a CUSTOM_NAME (i.e. clearing it); a null name is not a rename. In that case the handler returns and vanilla takes over - and vanilla cannot repair a Warp Stone with amethyst, so a repair+rename in one anvil operation yields NO output at all. Players must repair first and rename afterwards (the code comment at line 87 says exactly this). Identical logic to free_anvil_repair's isRenaming.

FREE-COST COUPLING (surprising, worth documenting): the zero-cost path depends on a DIFFERENT module. This module sets cost 0 when ModuleManager.getInstance().isModuleEnabled("free_anvil_repair") (WaystoneAmethystRepairModule.java:40 + :112). A zero-cost anvil output is otherwise un-takeable: vanilla's AnvilMenu.mayPickup is `(player.hasInfiniteMaterials() || player.experienceLevel >= cost) && cost > 0` (AnvilMenu.java:72-74) - cost 0 fails even in creative. What rescues it is free_anvil_repair's AnvilMenuFreeRepairMixin, which returns true at HEAD of mayPickup when the result slot is filled, getCost() == 0 and FreeAnvilRepairModule.allowFreePickup(). GOTCHA: the two gates read different sources. ModuleManager.isModuleEnabled(String) (ModuleManager.java:194-199) consults the runtime override map and otherwise moduleEnabledState, a snapshot written at registration (ModuleManager.java:70) and once more in initializeModules (ModuleManager.java:91-97), while allowFreePickup() -> AbstractModule.isModuleEnabled() -> resolveModuleEnabled(moduleId, config.isEnabled()) (AbstractModule.java:202-210) reads the LIVE per-module config. A /vpa runtime override moves both together (both check runtimeModuleOverrides first), but editing free_anvil_repair's `enabled` flag in the config file at runtime moves only the live value: the snapshot stays true while the live config reads false, so this module would still produce a cost-0 result that mayPickup then refuses - an output the player cannot take out. Derived from the code paths, not reproduced in game.

HANDLER ORDER vs free_anvil_repair IS NOT DETERMINED BY SOURCE ORDER. Both modules subscribe AnvilUpdateEvent at default priority and are registered on the bus in their onInitialize, so the bus order equals the module initialization order - and that comes from iterating registeredModules.values() (ModuleManager.java:91 and :104), a ConcurrentHashMap (ModuleManager.java:23). Its iteration order is hash-bucket order, NOT the order of the registerModule calls in VanillaPlusAdditions.java (:174 free_anvil_repair, :175 waystone_amethyst_repair), so which of the two handlers runs first cannot be read off the source. This only matters in one overlap case: if a user adds `waystones:warp_stone=minecraft:amethyst_shard` to free_anvil_repair's extra_repair_materials, BOTH handlers claim the combination and neither inspects event.getOutput() before overwriting it, so whichever runs last wins (free_anvil_repair = fully repaired, cost 0, boosted per-unit; this module = repair_percent_per_unit per shard). With the default configs the combination is this module's alone: free_anvil_repair bails because a Warp Stone + amethyst is neither isValidRepairItem nor an extra_repair_materials entry nor a plain sacrifice.

THE MODULE DOES NOT ALWAYS INITIALIZE, and the runtime toggle is asymmetric. ModuleManager.initializeModules only calls initialize() for modules that were enabled when the config was first read (ModuleManager.java:91-107), and only onInitialize registers the handler - so a module that started disabled stays dead even after /vpa module enable, which needs a restart. Turning it OFF works instantly: isModuleEnabled() is re-checked at the top of every AnvilUpdateEvent and resolves the live config plus any runtime override. What is true regardless of Waystones: there is NO mod-presence gate anywhere (no ModList.isLoaded, no shouldInitialize) - with the module enabled the handler is always registered, and it merely never matches because the configured id fails BuiltInRegistries.ITEM.containsKey (lines 133-145).

CONFIG RESOLUTION IS LAZY AND CACHED, so changes take effect on the next anvil update without a restart: resolveTargetItem (133-145) re-parses only when the config string stops equalling the cached one, isRepairMaterial/parseItems (124-158) only when the config list stops equalling the cached list. Unresolvable ids are treated as absent (target -> module inert, material -> entry skipped), each with a debug-only log line. Minor asymmetry: material entries are trimmed (entry.trim(), line 150), the target id is not - though both the target and the material validators already reject anything ResourceLocation.tryParse cannot parse, whitespace included.

NO JEI ENTRY: this module has no @JeiPlugin (the four in the repo belong to battle_dogs, cat_guardian, axolotl_guardian, tipped_arrows, plus free_anvil_repair's). FreeAnvilRepairJeiPlugin renders only that module's extra_repair_materials entries (FreeAnvilRepairJeiPlugin.java:59), so Warp Stone + amethyst shows up nowhere in JEI and is undiscoverable in game - the known "JEI cannot auto-discover code-only anvil repairs" limitation.

README NUANCE: "Inactive without the Waystones mod" (README.md:135) is only true for the DEFAULT config. target_item and repair_materials are plain registry ids, so this is really a generic "make damageable item X repairable with material Y in an anvil" module and works with any installed damageable item, Waystones or not. The README also does not mention repair_percent_per_unit or that the free price is borrowed from another module.

SIDE: "server" is the honest answer for behaviour - there is no rendering, no keybind, no Dist./Minecraft.getInstance() reference, nothing in vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json, and the authoritative result slot, the XP charge and the item consumption are all decided server-side and reach the client through the normal menu sync (result slot + AnvilMenu.cost DataSlot), so a vanilla client on a modded server sees and can take the repair. CAVEAT: the handler is on the common NeoForge.EVENT_BUS with no side gate, and ItemCombinerMenu.slotsChanged -> createResult (ItemCombinerMenu.java:109-114) has no side check either, so the client's own menu copy runs the same code when the server syncs the input slots; its locally computed values are then overwritten by the synced ones. Note for consistency: scripts/docgen/data/modules/free_anvil_repair.json classifies the same AnvilUpdateEvent pattern as "both".
